claim_adjudications.span: revenue and GAAP operating income rose while total operating expenses were roughly flat, so the incremental revenue carried through to operating profit
both GAAP parent-attributable and company-defined adjusted parent net income increased

The revenue increase is concentrated in investment advisory fees alongside a larger average AUM base, which is consistent with a bigger asset base generating more fee revenue, though the rows do not establish that as the cause
Net cash outflows remained negative but were smaller in magnitude, which is a directional improvement in organic flow without establishing positive organic growth
The effective fee rate excluding performance-based fees declined, which points to mix or pricing pressure

The market-appreciation contribution to AUM was smaller, so the AUM increase depended relatively more on the opening balance and less on market gains, making the asset base more sensitive to market direction
A meaningful part of the revenue improvement came from a swing in capital allocation-based income, a signed and market-sensitive line rather than a recurring fee stream
The income tax provision rose alongside higher pretax income, which is a larger expense rather than a reduced tax drag
The deduction for redeemable non-controlling interests was smaller, which flattered parent-attributable income relative to consolidated net income
the Q3-only model-delivery asset addition has no comparator and is explicitly not a net flow
revenue and GAAP operating income rose while total operating expenses were roughly flat, and both GAAP parent-attributable and company-defined adjusted parent net income increased
net cash flows remained negative, so organic growth is not established
